text: dsh-sentinel 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的条件监控与 agent 唤醒插件。它在服务端持续检查文件、命令输出、HTTP 响应、进程和端口状态，也可接收 Webhook 或监听其他会话的回合结束事件；条件变化后会向对应会话投递带有触发摘要的唤醒消息。订阅记录保存在插件自己的日志中，界面提供会话监控卡片、跨会话侧栏面板和独立仪表盘，支持查看状态与触发历史。适合需要等待部署、任务或其他 agent 会话完成后再继续工作的用户。监控与投递需要持续运行的 DSH 服务进程；可选通知 Webhook 需自行配置。

dsh-sentinel adds condition watches to DSH and wakes agents on file, command, HTTP, process, port, webhook, or session turn-end events. It persists subscriptions and shows watch state and trigger history in a web dock, sidebar panel, and standalone dashboard. Monitoring needs a resident DSH process.
我希望文件或服务状态发生变化时，DSH 能自动叫醒正在等待的 agent。
能不能等某个命令输出指定内容后再通知我？
想监控一个 HTTP 地址或端口，状态改变时恢复会话。
让一个 DSH 会话在另一个 agent 完成回合后接着处理。
我需要用 Webhook 从 CI 或其他机器触发 agent 继续工作。
DSH 可以记住文件监控订阅，并在服务重启后继续监控吗？
有没有地方能集中查看所有会话正在等待的条件？
Can an agent resume when a watched file or process changes?
I want to wake a session from a webhook or another session’s turn-end event.
Can I inspect active watches and their recent trigger history in a browser?
dsh-sentinel 的功能「七类监控」：sentinel_watch 可订阅文件、命令、HTTP、进程、端口、会话回合结束或 Webhook 条件，并设置匹配规则、间隔和触发次数。
dsh-sentinel 的功能「持久订阅与恢复」：服务端将订阅变化追加到插件日志，启动时折叠日志恢复状态，并在触发时向目标会话投递唤醒。
dsh-sentinel 的功能「查看与取消监控」：sentinel_list 显示当前会话的监控及状态，sentinel_cancel 按监控 ID 取消订阅。
dsh-sentinel 的功能「会话监控卡片」：Web 客户端在对话输入区显示当前会话的监控状态与触发信息。
dsh-sentinel 的功能「跨会话面板」：侧栏 Sentinel 面板展示服务端范围的监控表，并可选接入 better-sidebar 标签页。
dsh-sentinel 的功能「独立仪表盘」：浏览器仪表盘轮询服务端状态路由，展示监控和触发历史，并提供取消操作。
dsh-sentinel 的功能「匹配边沿触发」：可选正则在内容从不匹配转为匹配时触发；未提供正则时，在基线后的快照变化时触发。
dsh-sentinel 的监控与唤醒由常驻 DSH 服务进程驱动；一次性 headless 进程退出后不会继续探测或投递。
Monitoring and wakeup delivery require a resident DSH process; one-shot headless runs stop after exit.

dsh-sentinel README · dsh-sentinel：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Condition-driven wakeup for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): the agent registers a watch, goes to sleep — even closes the session — and the sentinel wakes it when the condition happens. Every subscription and every fire is a user-visible session event, and the browser dock shows what is on duty.

dsh-sentinel README · How it works：The node half owns one server-lifetime runtime that folds a plugin-owned sidecar log (`$DSH_HOME/sentinel.jsonl`) into live subscriptions, probes every probe sensor on a shared 5s heartbeat, observes every published session's durable `turn/end` event for `session` watches, and delivers wakeups through the official followup channel — resuming a dormant session's agent first when needed. Subscriptions therefore survive process restarts, and conditions that become true while the server is down late-fire on the next probe (session watches fire on the next observed turn end).

dsh-sentinel README · How it works：Watching is a resident-process concern: probing and fire delivery only run while a long-running dsh process (typically `dsh web`) is up. Headless one-shot runs load the plugin and can create, list and cancel watches, but nothing probes after the process exits — those watches become active once a resident process starts.

dsh-sentinel README · How it works：One duty owner per `$DSH_HOME`: a lease file (`sentinel.lease`) makes the first process own probing and delivery; a second dsh process on the same home stays passive (tools work, writes persist to the shared sidecar) and takes over within one lease TTL of the owner dying. The owner re-reads the sidecar every heartbeat, so watches created on a passive instance are adopted automatically. Delivery is at-least-once: a fire logged but not delivered before a crash is requeued on the next boot from its `delivered` watermark.

dsh-sentinel README · How it works：The browser half is a dock card above the composer (the `conversation.input.dock` family) listing the session's active watches — sensor, target, live probe state, fire budget, next-probe countdown — plus recent fire history when expanded. It polls the read-only state route and renders nothing when the session has no watches.

dsh-sentinel README · How it works：Two surfaces make the server-global watch set visible. A **Sentinel entry in the sidebar's global panel list** (`sidebar.panellist`, id `sentinel`) opens the watch table in the central column (`main`, the same id) — its glyph carries a state dot while any watch is active. The dashboard is a standalone table of every watch across every session: session (active/dormant), sensor, target, pattern, fire budget, last probe state, next probe.

dsh-sentinel README · Sensors：| Kind | Engine | Fires on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | path snapshot + inotify push | snapshot change (sub-second); accelerated by fs events |
| `command` | read-only shell line, probed on an interval | output/exit-code change |
| `http` | URL probed on an interval | status/body change |
| `process` | `pgrep -f` pattern, probed on an interval | match-set change |
| `port` | TCP connect to `[host:]port`, probed on an interval | reachability change (open/closed/timeout) |
| `webhook` | pure push | any POST to the returned hook URL |
| `session` | host session-event feed (no probing) | another session's `turn/end`; optional `pattern` filters the reason kind |

dsh-sentinel README · Sensors：With `pattern`, probe kinds fire on the no-match→match edge of that regex, webhooks accept only matching payloads, and session watches fire only when the ended turn's reason kind matches the regex (`completed`, `max-tokens`, `aborted`, `blocked`, `error`, `interrupted`, `forked`); without it, probe kinds fire on any change after the baseline, webhooks fire on any POST, and session watches fire on any turn end.

dsh-sentinel README · Sensors：Session watches make serial session chains possible without poking anything from a prompt: `{ "kind": "session", "target": "<other-session-id>", "note": "step 1 finished — you're up", "maxFires": 1 }` wakes the watching session when the target session finishes a turn, and `pattern: "^completed$"` requires a clean completion (a crashed or aborted session never satisfies it, so the chain stops). The event is the host's durable `turn/end`; no probe baseline or heartbeat is involved. A turn end that happens while no resident dsh process can observe events is not replayed later — use a probe-backed gate when a chain must survive total downtime.

dsh-sentinel README · Configuration：All deployment-tunable knobs live in the plugin's config schema (defaults in parentheses); override them on the bundle row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-sentinel
  name: dsh-sentinel
  config:
    locale: en                  # server messages: en (default) or zh; UI follows the host

Invalid values fail plugin load with a schema error rather than misbehaving at runtime.

dsh-sentinel README · Configuration：`notifyWebhookUrl` fans every fire out of the harness as a JSON POST (`{plugin, event, sessionId, id, kind, target, note, fireNumber, maxFires, summary, after}`) — point it at a Lark/WeCom/Slack bot or any receiver. Delivery is at-most-once: a failed POST warns in the log and never blocks the in-harness wakeup.

dsh-sentinel README · Localization：- The dock, global panel and optional better-sidebar tab follow the DSH language setting, including changes while they are open. They do not override it with the browser's language. English and Chinese are supported; other host languages follow their registered fallback chain to one of these dictionaries, with English as the final fallback.
- The optional better-sidebar bottom-workbench tab can retain the title captured when it was opened. Its content updates live, but that saved tab-header title may require closing and reopening the tab after a language change; Sentinel does not modify third-party tab state.
- Dashboard links carry the selected UI language as `?lang=en` or `?lang=zh`. A direct dashboard request negotiates supported `Accept-Language` ranges by quality (`q`) and request order, respecting explicit exclusions before wildcards. It uses the server `locale` when no preference is supplied, and English when no supplied preference is acceptable. The initial HTML and subsequent refreshes use the same language, including the page title, both table headers, sensor labels, timestamps and fire summaries.

dsh-sentinel README · Localization：For example, an English UI now shows `Snapshot changed (state: exit 0)` instead of `快照发生变化（状态: exit 0）`, regardless of the server's message language.

The standalone page uses [Mustache.js 4.2.0](https://github.com/janl/mustache.js/tree/v4.2.0) and a small document/page/partial hierarchy:

dsh-sentinel README · Localization：```text
templates/layouts/document.html  document metadata and asset links
  templates/dashboard.html      page structure and table headings
    templates/dashboard/watches.html  watch rows and their empty state
    templates/dashboard/fires.html    fire rows and their empty state

dsh-sentinel README · Localization：This is standard Mustache partial composition, not a custom inheritance extension. Small tags, badges and regex markup stay in their owning template instead of one-tag files. The server renders the complete initial tables; the browser reuses the same meaningful row partials and typed presentation models. All values use default Mustache escaping for text and quoted attributes; no raw-HTML slots, caller-provided templates or template functions are used. Missing keys follow standard Mustache semantics (empty output); model and template contract tests cover required presentation fields.

dsh-sentinel README · Localization：Styles live in [the standalone stylesheet source](src/dashboard.css), copied by the build to [the shipped CSS asset](lib/dashboard.css) and linked from the document layout. [The separate browser script](lib/dashboard.js) is loaded with `defer`. The layout links the existing packaged SVG icon, avoiding a browser fallback request to a missing favicon. There are no inline styles or executable inline scripts, runtime code generation, serialized functions or dependencies on the DSH browser boot context. Mustache is bundled into the node and browser entries. Nested templates, CSS, JavaScript and the [third-party license notice](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) are all included in the npm package; initial HTML and styling do not require JavaScript.

dsh-sentinel README · Tools：- `sentinel_watch` — register a watch: `kind` (`file`, `command`, `http`, `process`, `port`, `session` or `webhook`), `target`, optional `pattern`, `interval` (5–86400s, default 30; ignored for `session` and `webhook`), `note` (delivered verbatim with every wakeup), `maxFires` (default 1: one-shot), `cooldown` (default 60s), optional `ttl`. For `session`, `target` is the id of the session whose `turn/end` to observe.
- `sentinel_list` — active watches with live probe state.
- `sentinel_cancel` — cancel one watch by id.

dsh-sentinel README · Routes：- `GET /plugins/dsh-sentinel/state?sessionId=…` — read-only state for the dock and the sidebar panel (omit `sessionId` for every session).
- `GET /plugins/dsh-sentinel/dashboard` — the server-global watch table.
- `GET /plugins/dsh-sentinel/dashboard.js` — its self-contained browser script.
- `GET /plugins/dsh-sentinel/dashboard.css` — its standalone stylesheet.
- `GET /plugins/dsh-sentinel/icon.svg` — the existing package icon used as the page favicon.
- These three fixed assets support `HEAD` with no body, reject other methods with 405, and use their own MIME types, `nosniff` and revalidation rather than immutable caching.
- `POST /plugins/dsh-sentinel/hook?id=watch-N&s=<sessionId>` — webhook entry; put a `curl` into a CI job, git hook, or another machine's script to wake the agent. Watch ids are per session, so the `s` qualifier is what keeps two sessions' `watch-1` hooks from colliding (the tool hands out the full URL). URLs without `s` still work and resolve to the first matching webhook watch.
- `POST /plugins/dsh-sentinel/cancel?sessionId=…&id=watch-N` — manual cancel. The dashboard table and every UI row carry a ✕ that calls this, so a watch can

dsh-sentinel README · Routes：First-probe semantics: a pattern-less probe watch absorbs its first observation as the baseline (no fire), while a pattern probe watch whose target already matches fires on the first probe — the condition already holds. Session watches have no probe baseline at all: their first matching `turn/end` fires.

dsh-sentinel README · Compatibility：Verified against these harness versions (plugin loads, duty lease is held, web routes answer). Session watches require the host's root-scope `session/event` feed, which the supported 0.2.x line provides; on a host outside that range the watch would be accepted but never fire. Sidecar rollback note: a `sentinel.jsonl` containing session-watch rows (new `kind`, or `trigger.kind: "session"` on fired rows) is rejected by 0.13.2 and older readers — cancel those watches before downgrading.

dsh-sentinel README · Compatibility：- `0.2.1-rc.4` — 2026-11-02, live web deployment upgraded from `0.2.1-rc.2` together with the `v0.14.0` plugin (launcher backup + clean profile reinstall + automatic verify/rollback kept; rehearsed first on an isolated copy of the live profile): launcher `0.2.1-rc.4`, sentinel **0.14.0**, web-shell `0.2.0`; boot graph 72 rows, both client bundles served, duty lease and state route answer, zero skipped bundles / activation warnings, no host `@deepseek-ai` packages in the profile. `locale: zh` is configured in the profile patch for server messages. The deployment's own `check-sentinel-deploy.sh` returned `RESULT: PASS`.
- `0.2.1-rc.2` — 2026-10-19, live web deployment upgraded from `0.2.0-rc.2` (clean profile reinstall, launcher backup + tested rollback path kept): the plugin activates, holds the duty lease, serves its client half and answers the state route (71 boot rows, zero skipped bundles, terminal plugin still loaded). No source change was required — against real `0.2.1-rc.2` packages `tsc -b --noEmit` passes, all 76 tests pass, and the rebuilt `lib/` is byte-identical — so 0.13.2 is an alignment release: devDependencies pinned to `0.2.1-rc.2

dsh-sentinel README · Compatibility：Compatibility means the cordis loader entries, the `ctx.agents` followup channel, the declared slot seats, and the web routes keep working; file an issue if a harness version breaks any of them. Its harness imports (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`) are `peerDependencies` plus `devDependencies`: the running host supplies the single instance (a second copy owns a different `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER` symbol and breaks real tool calls), while the exact dev pins keep local typecheck/build on the verified line. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` and `react` stay peers, and `engines.dsh` declares the supported host range.

dsh-sentinel README · Install：One line through the official bundle channel:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-sentinel
```

Or straight from git (build artifacts are committed, so the git-source install runs no build):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:fuhefei/dsh-sentinel#v0.14.0"
```

dsh-sentinel README · Install：The tag in this example tracks the latest release; older tags pin older host lines, so check the [Releases](https://github.com/fuhefei/dsh-sentinel/releases) page (or drop the tag and follow `main`) before copying into a different dsh version.

Alternatively, add the node half manually through a patch-list configuration over the shipped base:

```yaml

dsh-sentinel README · cordis.patch.yml：- insert:
    - id: dsh-sentinel
      name: dsh-sentinel
```

The browser half ships in the same package (`./client`) and is injected by the Web UI's plugin loader.

dsh-sentinel README · Sidebar surface (0.1.5 and later)：The dock, the sidebar entry and the dashboard all work on a stock host: the entry registers into the official `sidebar.panellist` seat and its panel into the layout's `main` slot, with no host patch.

dsh-sentinel README · Sidebar surface (0.1.5 and later)：Through 0.1.2 the global view instead grew a branch under each watched session row, which needed the session-row holes the official tree never declared; that path is retired with `patches/session-row-holes.patch` kept only for those older trees. 0.1.5 dropped the hole, so a plugin built for it must use the panel seat above.

dsh-sentinel README · better-sidebar integration (optional)：When [dsh-better-sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) is installed in the same profile, sentinel registers its global watch table as a sidebar tab (`dsh-sentinel:watches`, in the **+** menu) through better-sidebar's documented `ctx.betterSidebar.registerTab` extension surface: every watch server-wide with live probe state, fire budgets and recent fire history, fed by one shared poller. No configuration needed; without better-sidebar the registration is silently skipped and the dock / panel / dashboard keep working as before.

dsh-sentinel README · Plays well with：Install [dsh-notification](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-notification) alongside sentinel and the whole wakeup loop reaches your desktop: sentinel wakes the agent, the agent works the turn, and the turn's completion fires a desktop notification — no integration needed, the two plugins compose on their own.

dsh-sentinel README · Develop：```sh
npm install
npm run build     # tsc -b + tsdown (node, host client and standalone dashboard assets)
npm test          # vitest: domain, sensors, React lifecycle, templates/browser, packed assets, e2e
```
